properties.title: Strait of Hormuz
properties.desc: Iran and Oman. Sole sea exit of the Persian/Arabian Gulf, carrying most Gulf oil and LNG exports.

properties.title: Bab el-Mandeb
properties.desc: Yemen, Djibouti and Eritrea. Southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route; exposed to Houthi attacks on shipping.

properties.title: Suez Canal
properties.desc: Egypt. 193 km long. Shortest sea link between Europe and Asia; closure forces ships round the Cape of Good Hope.

properties.title: Strait of Malacca
properties.desc: Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore. Narrows to 2.8 km at the Phillip Channel. Main oil route from the Gulf to East Asia.

properties.title: Bosphorus
properties.desc: Turkey. Narrowest 0.7 km. Only outlet of the Black Sea to the Mediterranean, governed by the 1936 Montreux Convention.

properties.title: Dardanelles
properties.desc: Turkey. Narrowest 1.2 km. Southern half of the Turkish Straits linking the Black Sea to the Aegean.

properties.title: Strait of Gibraltar
properties.desc: Spain, Morocco and Gibraltar (UK). Narrowest 14 km. Only link between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

properties.title: Taiwan Strait
properties.desc: China and Taiwan. Narrowest 126 km. Heavily trafficked, and the focus of cross-strait military tension.

properties.title: Lombok Strait
properties.desc: Indonesia. Narrowest 20 km. Deep-water alternative to Malacca for large tankers and bulk carriers.

properties.title: Sunda Strait
properties.desc: Indonesia. Narrowest 24 km. Links the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean between Java and Sumatra.

properties.title: Panama Canal
properties.desc: Panama. 82 km long. Links the Atlantic and Pacific; handles a large share of US east-coast to Asia trade.

properties.title: Cape of Good Hope
properties.desc: South Africa. Main alternative to Suez and Bab el-Mandeb when the Red Sea route is closed or unsafe.

properties.title: Danish Straits
properties.desc: Denmark and Sweden (Great Belt, Little Belt, Oresund). Only sea exit of the Baltic to the North Sea.

properties.title: Strait of Dover (English Channel)
properties.desc: United Kingdom and France. Narrowest 33 km. One of the world's busiest shipping lanes; also the Channel Tunnel route.

properties.title: Kerch Strait
properties.desc: Russia and Russian-occupied Crimea (Ukraine). Narrowest 3.1 km. Only link between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.

properties.title: Mozambique Channel
properties.desc: Mozambique and Madagascar. Narrowest 419 km. Carries traffic on the Cape route around southern Africa.

properties.title: Korea Strait (Tsushima)
properties.desc: Japan and South Korea. Links the East China Sea to the Sea of Japan and serves major Korean and Japanese ports.

properties.title: Drake Passage
properties.desc: Chile and Argentina. About 800 km wide. Open-ocean route between the Atlantic and Pacific and gateway to Antarctica.

properties.title: Cape Horn
properties.desc: Chile. Southern tip of South America; the sea route for ships too large for the Panama Canal.

properties.title: Straits of Tiran
properties.desc: Egypt and Saudi Arabia. 5-6 km wide. Gate to the Gulf of Aqaba and the ports of Eilat and Aqaba; its 1967 closure preceded the Six-Day War.

properties.title: Bering Strait
properties.desc: Russia and the United States. Narrowest 82 km. Gateway between the Pacific and the Arctic, and a growing Arctic route.

properties.title: Strait of Sicily
properties.desc: Italy, Tunisia and Malta. Divides the eastern and western Mediterranean; a route for migration and energy trade.
